title: Scoring Hitchcock's The Lodger: landing the commission and budget
summary: Jackson describes writing a live score for Hitchcock's silent film The Lodger, how he got the commission, learning notation software and the small budget.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I saw a recent addition to your website and that you’re going to do a film score for something in Syracuse?

Right. In about three weeks. I’m really excited about it. I got an opportunity to write a score for a Hitchcock silent film called “The Lodger.” So I finished it up in the summer, and I finally got all the parts ready and sent them out to the musicians and so we have a rehearsal the day before the premiere, and then we do play the music live in front of an audience —
With the film above us, so I’m pretty psyched to get connected to Hitchcock in this fashion.
How do you go about landing a commission like that or whatever you want to call it?

Well I met the artistic director’s wife and told her of my interest in it and my willingness to be a part of writing for a film or TV. It’s been something that I’ve kind of been looking for. And so I got a chance to speak to her husband and they asked me if I’d like to do it and I jumped at it. And so that started in basically February. So it’s been a great process, a learning process for me. Traveling and doing it has been unique as well, because I had been writing basically from the piano to sheet music, which nowadays everything is done © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

to a program. So I’m actually archaic at this point. But I’ll get up to speed with the various programs that are available to me on the next project, so I had some help in terms of getting it put into a program and then obviously I needed help to sync the music up with the film.
Ah. I know right where you’re at with that. Trying to learn Finale and that kind of stuff.
Did you have — not restrictions — but did they have to tell you well here’s our budget, here’s what we can do as far as musicians and so forth?

Absolutely. The budget was like ha-ha-ha — but it’s their budget that they have every year and obviously with the all the various events that they have going on I was happy to take it and the other musicians were willing to work with me, and for me I would have almost paid a little bit just to do it.

So the opportunity speaks volumes to my chance at something like this. So it’s a good learning process for me to go through and then also something to have a little cachet to show the people about my ability in this area.
